summary.en: Security forces in Kulgam engaged a Lashkar-e-Taiba cell, killing commander Lateef Ahmad Bhat and other attackers while recovering a body and weapon, and have intensified search operations. Maharashtra announced cash rewards of Rs 1.5 lakh for information on weapons looted by Naxalites, and over 1,000 CRPF personnel were redeployed from Chhattisgarh to Manipur, including the withdrawal of an anti-Naxal battalion for Manipur duties. Japan lowered its travel advisory for parts of Meghalaya, and the ISI revived a K‑2 plan that brings multiple terror groups into Punjab to target police. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrkene i Kulgam engasjerte en Lashkar-e-Taiba-celle, drepte kommandør Lateef Ahmad Bhat og andre angripere mens de gjenvant en kropp og et våpen, og har skjerpet søkeoperasjonene. Statlige myndigheter i Maharashtra kunngjorde kontantbelønninger på Rs 1.5 lakh for informasjon om våpen som er plyndret av naxalitter, og mer enn 1 000 CRPF-personell ble omplassert fra Chhattisgarh til Manipur, inkludert tilbaketrekning av et anti-naxal-bataljon for oppgaver i Manipur. Japan senket reiserådet for deler av Meghalaya, og ISI gjenopptok en K-2-plan som bringer flere terrorgrupper inn i Punjab for å angripe politiet. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
